newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower ahead of Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower ahead of Greenspan.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Tuesday in a further consolidation of the bourse's recent gains in cautious trade ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the U.S. Senate later in the day.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 5.98 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,400.12 at 0920 GMT, while the CAC-40 January futures contract was eight points lower at 2,404.
"We've had a nice rise. It's normal to retrace a bit," a trader said.
Brokers said the market was feeling cautious because Greenspan's remark in the autumn that the euphoria may be overdone roiled financial markets.
Shares in luxury goods group LVMH were down 1.67 percent at 1,470 francs after Lehman Brothers downgraded its rating on the stock to underperform from neutral.
Lehman analyst John Wakely wrote in a comment that LVMH may not have gotten a good price for the seven percent of Guinness Plc that it sold last week.

"The tone of positive press comment surrounding the company has all the hallmarks of a bubble about to burst and though we shy away from making value judgments, 30 times 1997 earnings and 20 times cashflow in our experience is only matched by Coca-Cola," he said.

But a Paris brokerage issued a note on Tuesday raising its objective for LVMH's stock to 1,880 francs over the next 12 months from 1,570 francs previously, citing gains in profitability expected to result from LVMH's recent acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS.

Shares in oil majors Elf Aquitaine and Total gave up some of Monday's gains fuelled by the dollar's rise. Elf shares were down 0.96 percent at 515 francs, while Total's stock eased 0.11 percent to 449 francs.

Shares in Eurotunnel extended Monday's 5.8 percent gain on higher 1996 revenues and expectations of the finalisation by March of details on a bank debt accord. The share was up 4.79 percent at 7.65 francs.
